messages:
Alex D: Heads-up — seeing a slow p95 latency drift on the long-context pools over the last 48h. Correlates with short spikes in kv.evictions_total and a falling kv.residency_pct. Not sure if it's fragmentation or a bad eviction heuristic. profile: https://perf.internal/runs/2938 :thinking:
Maria S: Can you paste the PromQL you used? sampling can hide short bursts — our default kv telemetry sample_rate is 10% which smooths peaks.
Alex D: Quick query I ran: 
```
sum(rate(kv_evictions_total{pool="long-context"}[5m])) by (pool)
/ 
sum(kv_resident_fragments{pool="long-context"}) by (pool)
```
but that's noisy. I also pulled a perf profile that shows a rising number of small fragments after ~5000 tokens.
Sam K: Interesting. Two hypotheses: 1) eviction policy favors LRU across mixed sessions and long sessions churn hot entries; 2) our fragment coalescer isn't running often enough so small fragments accumulate and stop being reused.
Nina (oncall): Be careful if we increase telemetry to 100% for a whole pool — cardinality and storage spike. For a targeted repro window it's fine for 1h tho. Suggest: sample 100% for the specific node set / instance group, not global.
Alex D: Agreed. I can flip a local sample flag for pool-id=lc-4 for 30m. Want actionable metrics added to dashboards: 1) kv.hitrate_last_5m (per-pool), 2) kv.fragment_count_by_size (buckets), 3) kv.eviction_rate_per_min, 4) kv.residency_pct_by_session_topk.
Maria S: Nice list. For fragment size histogram we should avoid per-session labels. Do histogram by size bucket + pool only. Then add a topk(tag=session_id, 10) drilldown panel that runs on demand.
perf-bot: nightly-profiling: regression detected in kv_compact_worker: 12% slower wall-time vs baseline (2026-03-17). Details: https://perf.internal/reports/compactor/2026-03-18
Sam K: That lines up — compactor slower => fragments live longer => reuse falls => evictions spike when memory pressure hits. A short-term mitigation: lower compaction interval to 30s for long-context pools and increase stage_coalesce_threshold. Longer-term: make compactor opportunistic during low gpu-util windows.
Alex D: For alerts, propose this rule: alert if (sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])) by (pool) > 20 and avg_over_time(kv_residency_pct[5m]) by (pool) < 65%) for 5m. Also add a dashboard sparklines panel showing simultaneous p95 latency, eviction rate, and residency to spot coupling.
Maria S: PromQL for the alert (draft):
```
(sum(rate(kv_evictions_total{pool="long-context"}[5m])) by (pool) > 20)
and
(avg_over_time(kv_residency_pct{pool="long-context"}[5m]) by (pool) < 65)
```
We should wrap into recording rules first.
Nina (oncall): I'll approve a short-term paging alert but prefer to mute noisy pools during known experiments. Add a runbook link to the alert with steps: increase compactor frequency, enable 100% sampling for 30m, collect topk sessions, rollback compactor change.
Alex D: I'll open a PR with: dashboard panels, recording rules, and a small compactor tweak behind a feature flag. Will also coordinate the 30m sample window.
Sam K: If you want, I can add a low-overhead derived metric: kv.active_fragments_estimate computed from sampled fragment ids using reservoir sampling — gives a stable trend without high cardinality.
Maria S: Yes please. That plus the histogram should make the pattern obvious. Thanks — let's reconvene after we collect one repro run. :thumbsup:
Nina (oncall): Sounds good. Tag me when you flip sampling so I can watch the infra.
Alex D: Will do. Thanks all.
